question.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)={y}^{2}$ on the disk of radius $2$ centered at the origin.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\pi \cdot {2}^{2}=4\pi .
$$

The average value of the function over a region $D$ is given by

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 2,\,0\le \theta <2\pi \}.
$$

Using the change of variables formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}{r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {\int }_{0}^{2}{r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,{[\frac{{r}^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta (4-0)\text{d}\theta  \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1}{2}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{[\theta -\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =2[(2\pi -0)-\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡4\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡0)] \\  & =2\cdot 2\pi  \\  & =4\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{4\pi }\cdot 4\pi =1.
$$
